messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Investigating: spike in 5xx and streaming disconnects for /v1/stream across gateway region-us-east1. Alert threshold breached at 11:42 UTC. Paging SRE oncall.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): I’m on it. seeing elevated 502/504s from gateway and client side aborts. paging eng-runtime and eng-platform.
Eng Runtime (Alexa): looking now — initial metrics: p50 streaming latency ~220ms, p95 spiked from 1.2s -> 6s, 5xx rate ~3.8% over baseline 0.1%.
Prod Support (Priya): @SRE Oncall several customers reporting aborted streams and partial responses, one has logs showing repeated "upstream reset by peer".
Eng Platform (Maria): checking load balancer — ALB shows increased 502/504 for long-lived connections. Backend instances show many keepalive resets.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): quick mitigation options: 1) increase gateway upstream timeout from 60s->120s 2) enable non-streaming fallback for clients using paged responses 3) throttle new streaming sessions to reduce KV cache pressure. Which do we want now?
Eng Runtime (Alexa): do 1 and 3 immediately. The runtime is hitting high KV cache churn — when many clients open short streams, KV eviction plus kernel OOM-ish behavior causes request failures. Throttling new streams by 20% should buy time.
Eng Platform (Maria): applying gateway timeout bump and adding a 20% admission throttle for /v1/stream in region-us-east1 now. rolling patch...
deploy-bot: config deploy started: gateway/timeout-bump -> rollout id r-202103.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): add a temporary route to fallback to /v1/paged for clients that honor it. Prod Support, please send guidance to affected customers.
Prod Support (Priya): Sending customer note now. ETA 5m. Message: "We're seeing intermittent stream disconnects in us-east1; as a temporary measure, we can offer paged responses or retry helpers. We'll follow up with incident details"
Eng Runtime (Alexa): quick debug note — seeing chunked-encoding partial frames logged as: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:41:58Z] conn_id=0x7ff upstream: reset, bytes_sent=1024, last_frame=\"chunked\"
[2026-03-15T11:42:05Z] handler: write error: broken pipe
```
This points to connection resets between gateway and runtime process, possibly due to max connections per process. Also saw "client_cancel" events correlate with these.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): Querying traces for a sample request id: r:abcd1234.@@alex: can you pull full span?
Eng Runtime (Alexa): span shows gateway->router->runtime sequence with long idle time at router (30s) before streaming resumes. Router logs show many buffered chunks waiting. Suggest disabling gateway buffering for streaming endpoints.
Eng Platform (Maria): disabling buffering for /v1/stream in us-east1 now. Also increasing upstream_conn_pool size on router from 100->200 for the region to reduce backpressure.
deploy-bot: config deploy completed: gateway/disable-buffering r-202104; router/pool-size r-202105.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): After mitigations metrics: 5xx down to 0.9%, p95 latency back to ~1.4s. Still seeing occasional client cancels ~0.6%.
Customer Success (Ethan): Customer A reports better behavior but some clients still see truncation. He needs a reproducible curl example to pass to their infra team.
Eng Runtime (Alexa): reproducible curl to simulate long streaming client (from within our VPC):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"repeat\"x\" 10000 times","stream":true}'
```
Look for early FIN or RST in tcpdump.
Prod Support (Priya): note added to incident timeline: customer A partially impacted, ~12% of their stream requests experienced mid-stream disconnects during window.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): next steps: Eng Runtime to investigate root cause (KV cache eviction and process-level connection limits) and produce a patch. Eng Platform to make admission control more robust (dynamic backpressure). We'll keep timeout bump and buffering disabled as temporary config for 24h.
Eng Runtime (Alexa): I’ll open a PR with conservative changes: better KV cache backpressure, more robust chunk flush handling, and guard against write errors turning into panics. Assigning to eng-runtime team.
Eng Platform (Maria): I'll prepare a runbook update for streaming backpressure and an automated admission throttle based on runtime queue length. Also will run a canary in eu-west-1 before broader rollout.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): assigning post-incident owner: @Alexa to own root cause and timeline. @Maria owns platform mitigations and runbook. I'll file incident postmortem and coordinate customer comms.
Prod Support (Priya): customers notified. Will follow up with detailed timeline once we have RCA.
Customer Success (Ethan): thx. Keep me posted if we need to escalate to enterprise SLA team.
Eng Runtime (Alexa): quick note: logs extracted from runtime for request r:abcd1234 show repeated EWOULDBLOCK at write() prior to reset; suggests socket backpressure not handled correctly. adding non-blocking fallback path in PR.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): Good catch. For now mitigation steps documented. Incident severity -> P2 (customer-visible but partial, mitigations in place). Will reopen to P1 if impact increases.
Prod Support (Priya): closing triage loop; will remain monitoring.
SRE Oncall (Ryan): last update — 5xx and disconnects trending down. Closing live triage at 12:17 UTC.
